**HMG-API 1.1.0-rc.2 is the second release candidate:** rc.1 plus fixes from a review, and the fix for wireless CarPlay dropping after a minute. 1.1.0 will be this code unless a blocker turns up. If you'd rather wait, stay on [1.0.2](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/releases/tag/v1.0.2): it's still the current release.

It comes with **Wireless CarPlay + Android Auto [2.2.0-rc.3](https://github.com/Open-HMG/hmgapi-wireless-cp-aa/releases/tag/v2.2.0-rc.3)** and **ADB [1.0.1-rc.1](https://github.com/Open-HMG/hmgapi-adb/releases/tag/v1.0.1-rc.1)** (as in rc.1). NEMESIS in the app menu is the same as in 1.0.2.

## What's fixed since 1.1.0-rc.1

- **Wireless CarPlay no longer drops after about a minute on some phones** (wireless 2.2.0-rc.3). The stock CarPlay app cut the phone's Bluetooth link at the start of each wireless session, and some phones then ended the session. The link now stays up. Thanks to conorlmcbride (wireless #5, #2). On the Niro EV, Carnival and Palisade this fix waits for a newer Car Report.
- **The wireless mod supports the US Ioniq 5 (2023 on) on 260903** (wireless 2.2.0-rc.3): no more "isn't for this head unit". Thanks to joelsmith (#1).
- **Uninstalling gives the boot scripts back exactly as they were.** Before, they came back close to stock but not always byte for byte.
- **No restart loop after a failed rollback.** If an apply was cut off (power lost) and rolling it back then failed, the head unit could have restarted at every start. It now restarts only after a rollback that finished.
- **The app says when over-the-air updates aren't blocked.** On a car where HMG-API's hooks don't run (no hook map for it yet), the car's own updates still download and install. The Updates page used to say HMG-API blocks them; it now says they aren't blocked there and points at the car's own switch.
- **Car Reports for the Sportage, Telluride, Niro EV, Carnival and Palisade** have the car's name in their title instead of "null", and mods that list cars by name accept them.
- **Car Reports leave out addresses from the network keeper's log**, as they already did elsewhere.
- **A mod turning the rear camera's guide lines off now asks you first**, like turning them on.
- Safety fixes in how HMG-API handles a mod's files: a mod can't make files outside its own folder readable, removing a mod never deletes what a link in its folder points at, and a mod's background service can't take over other files through its folder. Mod authors: `mkmodpkg.sh` refuses to package a folder with a signing key in it.
- The full list is in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/blob/v1.1.0-rc.2/CHANGELOG.md); what came in rc.1 is in [its notes](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/releases/tag/v1.1.0-rc.1).

## Installing

- **From 1.0.x, the beta or rc.1:** put `hmgapi-1.1.0-rc.2-update.zip` in `HMGAPI/updates/` on a USB stick, then HMG-API app → **Check USB updates**. Then restart the head unit once. Your mods and settings stay. To update the wireless mod too (and ADB, from 1.0.x or the beta), also put `wireless-carplay-aa-2.2.0-rc.3.zip` and `adb-1.0.1-rc.1.zip` in `HMGAPI/updates/`, pick them in Check USB updates, and **Apply changes**.
- **With NEMESIS:** unzip `hmgapi-1.1.0-rc.2-nemesis.zip` onto a stick and update from NEMESIS Manager's Package Store.
- **New install, or after a firmware update:** as in [Installing HMG-API](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/wiki/Installing-HMG-API), with `hmgapi-1.1.0-rc.2-usb.zip`.

## What to test

- The app shows **1.1.0-rc.2** and "Hooks on". Your mods still run after the update and a restart.
- **Uninstall and install again** (without `PURGE`): the head unit starts normally afterwards, and NEMESIS still starts.
- **Wireless CarPlay for 5 minutes or more**, with a call: it stays connected. HMG-API's log says "Bluetooth kept up for wireless CarPlay". Wired CarPlay still connects as before.
- **Wireless Android Auto on a drive**, as for rc.1.
- **Ioniq 5 on 260903:** the wireless mod installs without a warning; wireless CarPlay (music, Siri, a call) and Android Auto with turn-by-turn on the cluster.
- **On a car without a hook map:** HMG-API app → Settings → Updates says over-the-air updates aren't blocked.
- **Sportage, Telluride, Niro EV, Carnival or Palisade:** HMG-API app → Settings → **Check the map on this car**, restart, then a [Car Report](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/wiki/Car-Report). Its title should name your car.

## Known issues

- With Android Auto's turns in the car's own format, on-ramps still show the projection icon, so the AR HUD doesn't animate there (wireless #30).
- The rest are the same as in [1.0.0](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/releases/tag/v1.0.0). For example, a USB stick left in the port can start wired Android Auto and stop wireless from connecting. Take the stick out after installing.

## Going back to 1.0.2

The app won't install an older HMG-API over a newer one, so either:
- **With adb:** `adb push hmgapi-1.0.2-update.zip /data/local/tmp/`, then `adb shell hmgapid engine update-hmgapi /data/local/tmp/hmgapi-1.0.2-update.zip --force`. Restart the head unit.
- **Without adb:** uninstall HMG-API ([Uninstalling](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/wiki/Uninstalling), without `PURGE`, so your mods and settings stay), restart, then install [1.0.2](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/releases/tag/v1.0.2) as new.

Wireless 2.2.0-rc.3 needs HMG-API 1.1.0, so going back to 1.0.2 means going back to wireless 2.1.0 too: remove the mod in the app and apply, then install `wireless-carplay-aa-2.1.0.zip` from 1.0.2's release with Check USB updates.

## Reporting

A [Car Report](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/wiki/Car-Report), or [open an issue](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/issues/new/choose) with:
- your car;
- the head unit software (e.g. 260507 or 260903);
- the HMG-API version (1.1.0-rc.2) and the wireless mod's version;
- what you did and what happened.

Problems with wireless CarPlay or Android Auto go [in the mod's repo](https://github.com/Open-HMG/hmgapi-wireless-cp-aa/issues/new/choose). Please don't post your VIN, serial numbers or phone numbers; nothing needs them.
